messages:
marta: Quick sync — I put together a proposal for how we deprecate the dropout-enabled fastpaths and make the dropout-free fused QKV the default for inference. Short version: default to dropoutless fastpath, keep a compatibility shim behind a feature flag, and add guarded fallbacks for cache/kv-layout mismatches. Feedback?

kai: why deprecate the dropout-enabled path instead of leaving both? some models still expect noise in logits for sampling diversity.

marta: mostly cost/complexity. The dropout path forces extra branches in kernels and prevents some kernel-level optimizations (continuous batching + fuse reorder). We measured ~12% latency win and ~18% throughput on our 8k seq baseline when removing dropout gating. Also memory drops ~8% because we skip some intermediate masks.

james: can we preserve same sampling behavior? If we default to dropoutless, downstream callers that relied on inference-time dropout will see differences. We should: 1) surface an explicit config var, 2) add a runtime shim that emulates dropout by perturbing logits post-token if requested, but run the fused path otherwise.

sylvia: important: quantized + dropout interplay is messy. Our current quantization pipeline expects the dropout mask to be applied pre-quant ops in a few models. If we flip default we need to revalidate per-model quant artifacts. Who owns that matrix?

marta: good catch. Plan: require model manifest opt-in to legacy dropout semantics. Default manifests get the dropoutless fastpath. We'll add a manifest field: `inference_dropout_mode: [none|legacy-emulate]` and a runtime `compat_mode` flag.

runtime-bot: perf-summary: baseline(unfused) -> p50 21.8ms p95 68ms tokens/s 310; fused_no_dropout -> p50 19.2ms p95 60ms tokens/s 366; mem -8%. Data from 2071200000 perf job.

kai: sounds reasonable. On kernel API: we need a clear operator contract for KV cache layout and microbatch merge boundaries. The fused kernel assumes contiguous heads + packed qkv layout. If callers send fragmented KV updates (e.g., microbatching across sequences), we must either copy into contiguous staging or fall back. Copying kills perf.

marta: proposal: expose two kernel entrypoints: `attn_fused_qkv_no_dropout(contiguous=true)` which is the fastpath and errors if layout != expected, and `attn_fused_qkv_no_dropout_compat` which accepts fragmented layout but does internal copy. At runtime we route by `request.contiguous_kv_hint` (bool) and by `pooling_policy`.

james: agree but add a feature-guard at rollout: the fast entrypoint should be enabled only when model_manifest+runtime flags align and we pass a new canary test that validates byte-for-byte outputs for a 50k token prompt set.

sylvia: tests: add quant + eval checks: run sample generation under sampling/beam/temperature combos and ensure distribution shift < threshold (we'll define statistical metrics). Also add a determinism check for cache replays.

marta: rollout plan draft: 1) add kernel + compat shim (dev branch) 2) unit tests + microbench harness (kai) 3) internal canary 5% traffic for 48h comparing logs/qlogs + eval metrics (james) 4) if no regressions, flip default in runtime 1 week later and monitor 7d for perf & quality alerts.

james: what about fallback semantics on OOM or kernel assert? Should we auto-fallback to unfused? I think yes but only for retries, and we should tag traces so ops teams can reason about it.

marta: auto-fallback allowed only once per request; mark request with `fallback_reason` tag and increase sampling rate for traces. Also add an aggregator that emits per-model fallback rates; alert at >0.1%.

kai: microbatching: we need to clarify scheduling interactions with batcher. If batcher merges different models/variants we need to reject fused path unless model+variant match. Add compatibility check inside batcher.

sylvia: I'll audit the model manifest validator to ensure `inference_dropout_mode` is available for Dedicated/Private deployments too. Also propose a migration script to mark manifests that explicitly used dropout behavior.

marta: owners & action items: I'll open RFC follow-up PR with kernel prototypes + config sketch. Kai owns batching/entrypoint tests. James owns canary plan & dashboards (p50/p95/quality regression). Sylvia owns manifest + quant revalidation. Runtime-bot: please attach the perf job id to the RFC. :white_check_mark:

runtime-bot: perf job attached: perf/2071200000. Canary template created at infra/canaries/dropoutless-fused-v1.

marta: Thanks all — if no blockers I'll file the follow-up RFC this afternoon and schedule a sync next Tue. If you have edge cases post them here or add to the RFC doc.
